answer: Relic-link routing. Each agent's messages carry a forward-only path signature; peers accept traffic only if the path crosses a minimum number of disjoint relay clusters, verified locally as a prism splitting the route into independent segments. New identities start with one link and earn a summit of distinct cluster adjacencies only through sustained multi-cluster traffic. An attacker must operate live relays across many clusters simultaneously, paying hosting and latency costs proportional to cluster count rather than to identities minted.
